name: Performance Profiling Conventions
description: This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on performance profiling so output stays consistent and easy to review.
content:
This module governs the naming, structure, and style conventions expected when working on performance profiling so output stays consistent and easy to review.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to performance profiling (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. Document any non-obvious performance profiling decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. Keep performance profiling changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Prefer the simplest performance profiling approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
5. When performance profiling decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. When performance profiling guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
7. When multiple performance profiling strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
8. Prefer explicit, readable performance profiling solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
9. Before starting performance profiling work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated performance profiling concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of performance profiling correctness.
- Avoid introducing new performance profiling abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for performance profiling, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
